supplements.title: Martial Stances
supplements.rules: When you choose the Martial Artist subclass, take the Martial Stances sheet to track which stances your character knows. You can also track which stance you have active and your current Focus.

supplements.title: Stances
supplements.rules:
Stances are special body positionings that enable Martial Artists to attack, react, or defend in combat. Each stance grants your character a different ability, bonus, or feature while active.
You choose two stances from Tier 1 when you first take the Martial Artist’s subclass foundation card. Mark the circle next to each to indicate that your character knows and has access to them. Mark a new stance from your tier or below each time you gain a level.

supplements.title: Focus
supplements.rules: Focus represents your character’s poise, clarity, and control. Once per rest during a moment of calm, you can clear your mind and refocus your martial instincts. Clear your Focus track, then roll a number of d6s equal to your Instinct and gain Focus equal to the highest result rolled. You can hold a maximum of 6 Focus.

supplements.title: Shifting Into Stances
supplements.rules:
You can spend a Focus to shift into a martial stance and gain its effects. You can shift only into stances you’ve marked as known. When you shift into a stance, it’s considered your active stance until you drop out of it.
You can’t shift into or have more than one active stance at a time. Until you shift into a stance, you are not considered to be in a stance or to have an active stance.

supplements.title: Dropping Out of Stances
supplements.rules: If you are already in a stance when you shift into a different stance, you automatically drop out of the previously active stance. You also drop out of your active stance when you take Severe damage or mark your last Hit Point. Otherwise, you drop out of your active stance at the end of the scene. When you drop out of a stance, you lose any ongoing benefits it provides.

supplements.title: Beastform Options
supplements.rules:
When you use your “Beastform” feature, choose a creature category of your tier or lower. At the GM’s discretion, you can describe yourself transforming into any animal that reasonably fits into that category.
Beastform categories are divided by tier. Each entry includes the following details:
- Creature Category: Each category’s name describes the common role or behavior of creatures in that category (such as Agile Scout). This name is followed by a few examples of animals that fit in that category (in this example, fox, mouse, and weasel).
- Character Trait: While transformed, you gain a bonus to the listed trait. For example, while transformed into an Agile Scout, you gain a +1 bonus to your Agility. When this form drops, you lose this bonus.
- Attack Rolls: When you make an attack while transformed, you use the creature’s listed range, trait, and damage dice, but you use your Proficiency. For example, as an Agile Scout, you can attack a target within Melee range using your Agility. On a success, you deal d4 physical damage using your Proficiency.
- Evasion: While transformed, you add the creature’s Evasion bonus to your normal Evasion. For example, if your Evasion is usually 8 and your Beastform says “Evasion +2,” your Evasion becomes 10 while you’re in that form.
- Advantages: Your form makes you especially suited to certain actions. When you make an action or reaction roll related to one of the verbs listed for that creature category, you gain advantage on that roll. For example, an Agile Scout gains advantage on rolls made to sneak around, search for objects or creatures, and related activities.
- Features: Each form includes unique features. For example, an Agile Scout excels at silent, dexterous movement—but they’re also fragile, making you more likely to drop out of Beastform.

classes.classItems: A trophy from your first kill or a seemingly broken compass

hopeFeature.name: Hold Them Off
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope when you succeed on an attack with a weapon to use that same roll against two additional adversaries within range of the attack.
hopeFeature.short: Spend 3 Hope when you succeed on a weapon attack to use that roll against two additional adversaries within range.

features.name: Ranger’s Focus
features.rules:
Spend a Hope and make an attack against a target. On a success, deal your attack’s normal damage and temporarily make the attack’s target your Focus. Until this feature ends or you make a different creature your Focus, you gain the following benefits against your Focus:
- You know precisely what direction they are in.
- When you deal damage to them, they must mark a Stress.
- When you fail an attack against them, you can end your Ranger’s Focus feature to reroll your Duality Dice.
features.short: Spend a Hope and make an attack. On a success, deal normal damage and make the target your Focus until this ends or you choose a different Focus. Against your Focus: you know their exact direction; when you deal damage to them, they mark a Stress; when you fail an attack against them, you can end this feature to reroll your Duality Dice.

supplements.title: Ranger Companion
supplements.rules: When you choose the Beastbound Ranger subclass, take a companion sheet. This sheet is for tracking important information about your character’s companion and can be tucked beneath the right side of your character sheet for ease of viewing.

supplements.title: Step 1: Name Your Companion
supplements.rules: Work with the GM to decide what kind of animal you have as your companion. Give them a name and add a picture of them to the companion sheet.

supplements.title: Step 2: Write Their Evasion
supplements.rules: Fill in their Evasion, which starts at 10.

supplements.title: Step 3: Choose Their Companion Experience
supplements.rules:
Create two Experiences for your companion based on their training and the history you have together.
Start with +2 in both Experiences. Whenever you gain a new Experience, your companion also gains one. All new Experiences start at +2.
Example Companion Experiences
Bold Distraction, Expert Climber, Fetch, Friendly, Guardian of the Forest, Horrifying, Intimidating, Loyal Until the End, Navigation, Nimble, Nobody Left Behind, On High Alert, Protective, Royal Companion, Scout, Service Animal, Trusted Mount, Vigilant, We Always Find Them, You Can’t Hit What You Can’t Find

supplements.title: Step 4: Choose Their Attack and Record Damage Die
supplements.rules: Finally, describe your companion’s method of dealing damage (their standard attack) and record it in the “Attack & Damage” section. At level 1, your companion’s damage die is a d6 and their range is Melee. Choose whether they deal physical or magic damage.

supplements.title: Your Companion
supplements.rules: The following sections will run you through the basics of working with your companion.

supplements.title: Using Spellcast Rolls, Hope, and Experiences
supplements.rules: Make a Spellcast Roll to connect with your companion and command them to take action. Spend a Hope to add an applicable Companion Experience to the roll. On a success with Hope, if your next action builds on their success, you gain advantage on the roll.

supplements.title: Attacking with Your Companion
supplements.rules: When you command your companion to attack, they gain any benefits that would normally only apply to you (such as the effects of “Ranger’s Focus”). On a success, their damage roll uses your Proficiency and their damage die.

supplements.title: Taking Damage as Stress
supplements.rules:
- When your companion would take any amount of damage, they mark a Stress. When they mark their last Stress, they drop out of the scene (by hiding, fleeing, or a similar action). They remain unavailable until the start of your next long rest, where they return with 1 Stress cleared.
- When you choose a downtime move that clears Stress on yourself, your companion clears an equal number of Stress.

supplements.title: Leveling Up Your Companion
supplements.rules:
When your character levels up, choose one available option for your companion from the following list and mark it on your sheet:
- Intelligent: Your companion gains a permanent +1 bonus to a Companion Experience of your choice.
- Light in the Dark: Use this as an additional Hope slot your character can mark.
- Creature Comfort: Once per rest, when you take time during a quiet moment to give your companion love and attention, you can gain a Hope or you can both clear a Stress.
- Armored: When your companion takes damage, you can mark one of your Armor Slots instead of marking one of their Stress.
- Vicious: Increase your companion’s damage dice or range by one step (d6 to d8, Close to Far, etc.).
- Resilient: Your companion gains an additional Stress slot.
- Bonded: When you mark your last Hit Point, your companion rushes to your side to comfort you. Roll a number of d6s equal to the unmarked Stress slots they have and mark them. If any roll a 6, your companion helps you up. Clear your last Hit Point and return to the scene.
- Aware: Your companion gains a permanent +2 bonus to their Evasion.

classes.name: Rogue
classes.classItems: A set of forgery tools or a grappling hook

hopeFeature.name: Rogue’s Dodge
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope to gain a +2 bonus to your Evasion until the next time an attack succeeds against you. Otherwise, this bonus lasts until your next rest.
hopeFeature.short: Spend 3 Hope for +2 Evasion until an attack next succeeds against you; otherwise it lasts until your next rest.

features.name: Cloaked
features.rules: Any time you would be Hidden, you are instead Cloaked. In addition to the benefits of the Hidden condition, while Cloaked you remain unseen if you are stationary when an adversary moves to where they would normally see you. After you make an attack or end a move within line of sight of an adversary, you are no longer Cloaked.
features.short: When you would be Hidden, you are Cloaked instead: the benefits of Hidden, and you stay unseen if stationary when an adversary moves to where they would see you. You stop being Cloaked after you attack or end a move in an adversary’s line of sight.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.rules:
When you succeed on an attack while Cloaked or while an ally is within Melee range of your target, add a number of d6s equal to your tier to your damage roll.
- Level 1 → Tier 1
- Levels 2–4 → Tier 2
- Levels 5–7 → Tier 3
- Levels 8–10 → Tier 4
features.short: When you succeed on an attack while Cloaked or while an ally is within Melee range of your target, add d6s equal to your tier to the damage roll (level 1: Tier 1; 2–4: Tier 2; 5–7: Tier 3; 8–10: Tier 4).

hopeFeature.name: Life Support

features.name: Prayer Dice
features.rules: At the beginning of each session, roll a number of d4s equal to your subclass’s Spellcast trait and place them on your character sheet in the space provided. These are your Prayer Dice. You can spend any number of Prayer Dice to aid yourself or an ally within Far range. You can use a spent die’s value to reduce incoming damage, add to a roll’s result after the roll is made, or gain Hope equal to the result. At the end of each session, clear all unspent Prayer Dice.
features.short: At the start of each session, roll d4s equal to your subclass’s Spellcast trait and place them on your sheet. Clear unspent dice at session end.

classes.classItems: A whispering orb or a family heirloom

hopeFeature.name: Volatile Magic
hopeFeature.rules: Spend 3 Hope to reroll any number of your damage dice on an attack that deals magic damage.
hopeFeature.short: Spend 3 Hope to reroll any number of damage dice on an attack that deals magic damage.

features.name: Arcane Sense
features.rules: You can sense the presence of magical people and objects within Close range.
features.short: Sense magical people and objects within Close range.

features.name: Minor Illusion
features.rules: Make a Spellcast Roll (10). On a success, you create a minor visual illusion no larger than yourself within Close range. This illusion is convincing to anyone at Close range or farther.
features.short: Spellcast Roll (10): create a minor visual illusion no larger than yourself within Close range, convincing to anyone at Close range or farther.

features.name: Channel Raw Power
features.rules:
Once per long rest, you can place a domain card from your loadout into your vault and choose to either:
- Gain Hope equal to the level of the card.
- Enhance a spell that deals damage, gaining a bonus to your damage roll equal to twice the level of the card.
features.short: Once per long rest, move a domain card from your loadout to your vault and either gain Hope equal to its level, or enhance a damage spell for a bonus to the damage roll equal to twice its level.

classes.classItems: A carving that symbolizes your patron or a ring you can’t remove

hopeFeature.name: Patron’s Boon
hopeFeature.rules: When you fail a roll, you can spend 3 Hope to reroll with advantage.

features.name: Patron’s Pact
features.rules: You have committed yourself to a supernatural entity —such as a god, fae, or demon—in exchange for power. Write their name on your character sheet, then work with your GM to determine their sphere of influence (such as Nature, Chaos, Wisdom, Mischief, Love, War, Justice, or Death). Before making an action roll that relates to your patron’s sphere of influence, you can spend a Favor to call upon their aid, rolling your Patron Die and adding its result to the total. Your Patron Die starts at a d6 and increases to a d8 at level 5.
features.short: You are committed to a supernatural entity (a god, fae, demon, etc.) in exchange for power. features.name: Attack of Opportunity
features.rules:
If an adversary within Melee range attempts to leave that range, make a reaction roll using a trait of your choice against their Difficulty. Choose one effect on a success, or two if you critically succeed:

- You deal damage to them equal to your primary weapon’s damage.

- Ghost Petal: The target becomes temporarily Vulnerable.
- Grave Spore: The target must also mark a Stress.
- Leech Weed: You deal an extra 1d6 damage on this attack.

features.rules: You are immune to poisons and other toxins.
features.short: You are immune to poisons and other toxins.

features.name: Gifted Performer

You can play three different types of songs, once each per long rest; describe how you perform for others to gain the listed benefit:
- Relaxing Song: You and all allies within Close range clear a Hit Point.
- Epic Song: Make a target within Close range temporarily Vulnerable.
- Heartbreaking Song: You and all allies within Close range gain a Hope.
features.short: Describe your performance to play each song once per long rest: Relaxing (you and allies within Close range clear a Hit Point), Epic (a target within Close range is temporarily Vulnerable), Heartbreaking (you and allies within Close range gain a Hope).

features.rules: Maestro. Your rallying songs steel the courage of those who listen. When you give a Rally Die to an ally, they can gain a Hope or clear a Stress.
features.short: Maestro. When you give an ally a Rally Die, they can gain a Hope or clear a Stress.

features.short: Virtuoso. Perform each Gifted Performer song twice per long rest.

features.name: Rousing Speech
features.rules: Once per long rest, you can give a heartfelt, inspiring speech. All allies within Far range clear 2 Stress.
features.short: Once per long rest, give a speech: all allies within Far range clear 2 Stress.

features.name: Heart of a Poet
features.rules: After you make an action roll to impress, persuade, or offend someone, you can spend a Hope to add a d4 to the roll.
features.short: After an action roll to impress, persuade, or offend, spend a Hope to add a d4.

features.rules:

- Allow them to find a mundane object or tool they need.
- Help an Ally without spending Hope.
- Give them an additional downtime move during their next rest.
features.short: Eloquent. Once per session, when you encourage an ally, choose one: they find a mundane object or tool they need; Help an Ally without spending Hope; or they get an additional downtime move next rest.

features.rules: Epic Poetry. Your Rally Die increases to a d10. Additionally, when you Help an Ally, you can narrate the moment as if you were writing the tale of their heroism in a memoir. When you do, roll a d10 as your advantage die.
features.short: Epic Poetry. Your Rally Die is a d10. When you Help an Ally, you can narrate it as the tale of their heroism and roll a d10 as your advantage die.

features.name: Rugged

features.short: Permanent +3 to your Severe damage threshold.

features.name: Overwhelm

features.short: On a successful attack, spend a Hope to throw the target (within Close range) or force them to mark a Stress.

features.rules: When you make an attack with a Melee weapon, you can spend any number of Hope to target an equal number of additional creatures within Melee range.
features.short: When you attack with a Melee weapon, spend any number of Hope to target that many additional creatures within Melee range.

features.short: Once per rest, when an adversary within Melee range forces you to mark Hit Points, mark a Stress to force them to mark the same number.

features.name: Not Done Yet

features.short: When you take Severe damage, gain a Hope or clear a Stress.

features.rules: Take the Martial Stances sheet and choose two martial stances from Tier 1. Each time you level up your character, choose an additional stance from your tier or lower.

features.name: Keen Defenses
features.rules: When you’re targeted by an attack, you can spend a Focus to gain a bonus to your Evasion equal to your tier against the attack.
features.short: When targeted by an attack, spend a Focus for a bonus to Evasion equal to your tier against it.

features.name: Focus Cannon
features.rules: Spend a Focus to make an Instinct Roll against an adversary within Far range. On a success, deal d20+3 magic damage using your Proficiency.
features.short: Spend a Focus to make an Instinct Roll against an adversary within Far range. On a success, deal d20+3 magic damage using your Proficiency.

features.name: Limit Breaker
features.rules: Once per rest, you can perform an unbelievable feat of athletic prowess, such as running across water, leaping between distant rooftops, or scaling a building without needing to roll. When you do, gain a Hope and clear a Stress.
features.short: Once per rest, perform an unbelievable athletic feat (run across water, leap between rooftops, scale a building) without rolling; gain a Hope and clear a Stress.

features.name: Flow State
features.rules: You can mark a Stress instead of spending a Focus to shift into a different stance. Additionally, you can spend a Focus instead of marking a Stress to start a combo strike.
features.short: Mark a Stress instead of spending a Focus to change stance. Spend a Focus instead of marking a Stress to start a combo strike.

features.name: Elemental Incarnation
features.rules:
Mark a Stress to Channel one of the following elements until you take Severe damage or until your next rest:
- Fire: When an adversary within Melee range deals damage to you, they take 1d10 magic damage.
- Earth: Gain a bonus to your damage thresholds equal to your Proficiency.
- Water: When you deal damage to an adversary within Melee range, all other adversaries within Very Close range must mark a Stress.
- Air: You can hover, gaining advantage on Agility Rolls.
features.short: Mark a Stress to Channel an element until you take Severe damage or next rest (see the Elements table on the domain card sheet).

rows.name: Fire
rows.short: Adversaries in Melee range that damage you take 1d10 magic damage.

rows.name: Earth
rows.short: Add your Proficiency to your damage thresholds.

rows.name: Water
rows.short: When you damage an adversary in Melee range, all others within Very Close range mark a Stress.

features.name: Elemental Aura
features.rules:
Once per rest while Channeling, you can assume an aura matching your element. The aura affects targets within Close range until your Channeling ends.
- Fire: When an adversary marks 1 or more Hit Points, they must also mark a Stress.
- Earth: Your allies gain a +1 bonus to Strength.
- Water: When an adversary deals damage to you, you can mark a Stress to move them anywhere within Very Close range of where they are.
- Air: When you or an ally takes damage from an attack beyond Melee range, reduce the damage by 1d8.
features.short: Once per rest while Channeling, assume an aura affecting targets within Close range until Channeling ends (see the Elements table).

rows.name: Fire
rows.short: Adversaries that mark Hit Points also mark a Stress.

rows.name: Water
rows.short: When an adversary damages you, mark a Stress to move them anywhere within Very Close range of where they are.

rows.name: Air
rows.short: When you or an ally takes damage from an attack beyond Melee range, reduce it by 1d8.

features.name: Elemental Dominion
features.rules:
You further embody your element. While Channeling, you gain the following benefit:
- Fire: You gain a +1 bonus to your Proficiency for attacks and spells that deal damage.
- Earth: When you would mark Hit Points, roll a d6 per Hit Point marked. For each result of 6, reduce the number of Hit Points you mark by 1.
- Water: When an attack against you succeeds, you can mark a Stress to make the attacker temporarily Vulnerable.
- Air: You gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion and can fly.
features.short: While Channeling, gain your element’s benefit (see the Elements table).

rows.name: Fire
rows.short: +1 Proficiency for attacks and spells that deal damage.

rows.name: Earth
rows.short: When you would mark Hit Points, roll a d6 per Hit Point; each 6 reduces the number marked by 1.

rows.name: Water
rows.short: When an attack against you succeeds, mark a Stress to make the attacker temporarily Vulnerable.

features.name: Clarity of Nature
features.rules: Once per long rest, you can create a space of natural serenity within Close range. When you spend a few minutes resting within the space, clear Stress equal to your Instinct, distributed as you choose between you and your allies.
features.short: Once per long rest, create a space of natural serenity within Close range. After a few minutes resting there, clear Stress equal to your Instinct, split as you choose between you and allies.

features.name: Regeneration
features.rules: Touch a creature and spend 3 Hope. That creature clears 1d4 Hit Points.
features.short: Touch a creature and spend 3 Hope: it clears 1d4 Hit Points.

features.name: Regenerative Reach
features.rules: You can target creatures within Very Close range with your “Regeneration” feature.
features.short: Regeneration can target creatures within Very Close range.

features.name: Warden’s Protection
features.rules: Once per long rest, spend 2 Hope to clear 2 Hit Points on 1d4 allies within Close range.
features.short: Once per long rest, spend 2 Hope to clear 2 Hit Points on 1d4 allies within Close range.

features.name: Defender
features.rules: Your animal transformation embodies a healing guardian spirit. When you’re in Beastform and an ally within Close range marks 2 or more Hit Points, you can mark a Stress to reduce the number of Hit Points they mark by 1.
features.short: In Beastform, when an ally within Close range marks 2 or more Hit Points, mark a Stress to reduce the number they mark by 1.

features.name: Unwavering
features.rules: Gain a permanent +1 bonus to your damage thresholds.
features.short: Permanent +1 to your damage thresholds.

features.name: Iron Will
features.rules: When you take physical damage, you can mark an additional Armor Slot to reduce the severity.
features.short: When you take physical damage, you can mark an additional Armor Slot to reduce its severity.

features.name: Unrelenting
features.rules: Gain a permanent +2 bonus to your damage thresholds.
features.short: Permanent +2 to your damage thresholds.

features.name: Partners-in-Arms
features.rules: When an ally within Very Close range takes damage, you can mark an Armor Slot to reduce the severity by one threshold.
features.short: When an ally within Very Close range takes damage, mark an Armor Slot to reduce its severity by one threshold.

features.name: Undaunted
features.rules: Gain a permanent +3 bonus to your damage thresholds.
features.short: Permanent +3 to your damage thresholds.

features.name: Loyal Protector
features.rules: When an ally within Close range has 2 or fewer Hit Points and would take damage, you can mark a Stress to sprint to their side and take the damage instead.
features.short: When an ally within Close range with 2 or fewer Hit Points would take damage, mark a Stress to sprint to their side and take it instead.

features.name: At Ease
features.rules: Gain an additional Stress slot.
features.short: Gain an additional Stress slot.

features.name: Revenge
features.rules: When an adversary within Melee range succeeds on an attack against you, you can mark 2 Stress to force the attacker to mark a Hit Point.
features.short: When an adversary within Melee range hits you, mark 2 Stress to force it to mark a Hit Point.

features.name: Act of Reprisal
features.rules: When an adversary damages an ally within Melee range, you gain a +1 bonus to your Proficiency for the next successful attack you make against that adversary.
features.short: When an adversary damages an ally within Melee range, +1 Proficiency on your next successful attack against it.

features.name: Nemesis
features.rules: Spend 2 Hope to Prioritize an adversary until your next rest. When you make an attack against your Prioritized adversary, you can swap the results of your Hope and Fear Dice. You can only Prioritize one adversary at a time.
features.short: Spend 2 Hope to Prioritize an adversary until your next rest (one at a time). When you attack it, you can swap your Hope and Fear Dice results.

features.name: Companion
features.rules: You have an animal companion of your choice (at the GM’s discretion). They stay by your side unless you tell them otherwise.
features.short: You have an animal companion (GM’s discretion) who stays by your side unless you say otherwise.

features.rules: Take the Ranger Companion sheet. When you level up your character, choose a level-up option for your companion from this sheet as well.
features.short: Take the Ranger Companion sheet. When you level up, also choose a level-up option for your companion.

features.name: Expert Training
features.rules: Choose an additional level-up option for your companion.
features.short: Choose an additional companion level-up option.

features.name: Battle-Bonded
features.rules: When an adversary attacks you while they’re within your companion’s Melee range, you gain a +2 bonus to your Evasion against the attack.
features.short: When an adversary attacks you within your companion’s Melee range, +2 Evasion against the attack.

statNote.text: +2 Evasion against an attack from within your companion’s Melee range.

features.name: Advanced Training
features.rules: Choose two additional level-up options for your companion.
features.short: Choose two additional companion level-up options.

features.name: Loyal Friend
features.rules: Once per long rest, when the damage from an attack would mark your companion’s last Stress or your last Hit Point and you’re within Close range of each other, you or your companion can rush to the other’s side and take that damage instead.
features.short: Once per long rest, when damage would mark your companion’s last Stress or your last Hit Point and you’re within Close range of each other, either of you can rush to the other’s side and take it instead.

features.name: Ruthless Predator
features.rules: When you make a damage roll, you can mark a Stress to gain a +1 bonus to your Proficiency. Additionally, when you deal Severe damage to an adversary, they must mark a Stress.
features.short: When you make a damage roll, mark a Stress for +1 Proficiency. When you deal Severe damage to an adversary, they mark a Stress.

features.name: Path Forward
features.rules: When you’re traveling to a place you’ve previously visited or you carry an object that has been at the location before, you can identify the shortest, most direct path to your destination.
features.short: When traveling to a place you’ve visited, or carrying an object that has been there, you can identify the shortest, most direct path.

features.name: Elusive Predator
features.rules: When your Focus makes an attack against you, you gain a +2 bonus to your Evasion against the attack.
features.short: When your Focus attacks you, +2 Evasion against the attack.

statNote.text: +2 Evasion against an attack from your Focus target.

features.name: Apex Predator
features.rules: Before you make an attack roll against your Focus, you can spend a Hope. On a successful attack, you remove a Fear from the GM’s Fear pool.
features.short: Before you attack your Focus, you can spend a Hope. On a success, remove a Fear from the GM’s Fear pool.

features.name: Shadow Stepper
features.rules: You can move from shadow to shadow. When you move into an area of darkness or a shadow cast by another creature or object, you can mark a Stress to disappear from where you are and reappear inside another shadow within Far range. When you reappear, you are Cloaked.
features.short: When you move into darkness or another creature’s or object’s shadow, mark a Stress to vanish and reappear in another shadow within Far range, Cloaked.

features.name: Dark Cloud
features.rules: Make a Spellcast Roll (15). On a success, create a temporary dark cloud that covers any area within Close range. Anyone in this cloud can’t see outside of it, and anyone outside of it can’t see in. You’re considered Cloaked from any adversary for whom the cloud blocks line of sight.
features.short: Spellcast Roll (15): create a temporary dark cloud over an area within Close range. No one can see into or out of it, and you’re Cloaked from any adversary it blocks.

features.name: Adrenaline
features.rules: While you're Vulnerable, add your level to your damage rolls.
features.short: While Vulnerable, add your level to your damage rolls.

features.name: Fleeting Shadow
features.rules: Gain a permanent +1 bonus to your Evasion. You can use your “Shadow Stepper” feature to move within Very Far range.
features.short: Permanent +1 Evasion. Shadow Stepper works within Very Far range.

features.name: Vanishing Act
features.rules: Mark a Stress to become Cloaked at any time. When Cloaked from this feature, you automatically clear the Restrained condition if you have it. You remain Cloaked in this way until you roll with Fear or until your next rest.
features.short: Mark a Stress to become Cloaked at any time, and automatically clear Restrained. You stay Cloaked this way until you roll with Fear or your next rest.

features.name: Well-Connected
features.rules:
When you arrive in a prominent town or environment, you know somebody who calls this place home. Give them a name, note how you think they could be useful, and choose one fact from the following list:
- They owe me a favor, but they’ll be hard to find.
- They’re going to ask for something in exchange.
- They’re always in a great deal of trouble.
- We used to be together. It’s a long story.
- We didn’t part on great terms.
features.short: When you arrive in a prominent town or environment, you know someone who lives there. Name them, note how they could help, and choose one: they owe you a favor but are hard to find; they’ll want something in exchange; they’re always in trouble; you used to be together; you didn’t part on good terms.

features.name: Contacts Everywhere
features.rules:
Once per session, you can briefly call on a shady contact. Choose one of the following benefits and describe what brought them here to help you in this moment:
- They provide 1 handful of gold, a unique tool, or a mundane object that the situation requires.
- On your next action roll, their help provides a +3 bonus to the result of your Hope or Fear Die.
- The next time you deal damage, they snipe from the shadows, adding 2d8 to your damage roll.
features.short: Once per session, call on a shady contact and choose one: 1 handful of gold, a unique tool, or a mundane object the situation needs; +3 to the result of your next action roll’s Hope or Fear Die; the next time you deal damage, they add 2d8 to it.

features.name: Reliable Backup
features.rules:
You can use your “Contacts Everywhere” feature three times per session. The following options are added to the list of benefits you can choose from when you use that feature:
- When you mark 1 or more Hit Points, they can rush out to shield you, reducing the Hit Points marked by 1.
- When you make a Presence Roll in conversation, they back you up. You can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.
features.short: Use Contacts Everywhere three times per session. Added options: when you mark Hit Points, they reduce the Hit Points marked by 1; when you make a Presence Roll in conversation, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.

features.name: Spirit Weapon
features.rules: When you have an equipped weapon with a range of Melee or Very Close, it can fly from your hand to attack an adversary within Close range and then return to you. You can mark a Stress to target an additional adversary within range with the same attack roll.
features.short: An equipped Melee or Very Close weapon can fly from your hand to attack an adversary within Close range and return. Mark a Stress to target an additional adversary within range with the same roll.

features.name: Sparing Touch
features.rules: Once per long rest, touch a creature and clear 2 Hit Points or 2 Stress from them.
features.short: Once per long rest, touch a creature and clear 2 Hit Points or 2 Stress from them.

features.name: Devout
features.rules: When you roll your Prayer Dice, you can roll an additional die and discard the lowest result. Additionally, you can use your “Sparing Touch” feature twice instead of once per long rest.
features.short: When you roll Prayer Dice, roll an additional die and discard the lowest. Use Sparing Touch twice per long rest.

features.name: Sacred Resonance
features.rules: When you roll damage for your “Spirit Weapon” feature, if any of the die results match, double the value of each matching die. For example, if you roll two 5s, they count as two 10s.
features.short: When you roll Spirit Weapon damage, matching dice double their value (two 5s count as two 10s).

features.name: Wings of Light
features.rules:
You can fly. While flying, you can do the following:
- Mark a Stress to pick up and carry another willing creature approximately your size or smaller.
- Spend a Hope to deal an extra 1d8 damage on a successful attack.
features.short: You can fly. While flying: mark a Stress to carry another willing creature of about your size or smaller; spend a Hope to deal an extra 1d8 damage on a successful attack.

features.name: Ethereal Visage
features.rules: Your supernatural visage strikes awe and fear. While flying, you have advantage on Presence Rolls. When you succeed with Hope on a Presence Roll, you can remove a Fear from the GM’s Fear pool instead of gaining Hope.
features.short: While flying, advantage on Presence Rolls. When you succeed with Hope on a Presence Roll, you can remove a Fear from the GM’s Fear pool instead of gaining Hope.

features.name: Ascendant
features.rules: Gain a permanent +4 bonus to your Severe damage threshold.
features.short: Permanent +4 to your Severe damage threshold.

features.name: Power of the Gods
features.rules: While flying, you deal an extra 1d12 damage instead of 1d8 from your “Wings of Light” feature.
features.short: While flying, Wings of Light deals an extra 1d12 instead of 1d8.

features.name: Elementalist
features.rules: Choose one of the following elements at character creation: air, earth, fire, lightning, water.
features.short: At character creation, choose an element: air, earth, fire, lightning, or water. You can shape it into harmless effects. Spend a Hope and describe how your control of it helps an action roll you’re about to make, for +2 to the roll or +3 to its damage.

features.rules: You can shape this element into harmless effects.
Additionally, spend a Hope and describe how your control over this element helps an action roll you’re about to make, then either gain a +2 bonus to the roll or a +3 bonus to the roll’s damage.

features.name: Natural Evasion
features.rules: You can call forth your element to protect you from harm. When an attack roll against you succeeds, you can mark a Stress and describe how you use your element to defend you. When you do, roll a d6 and add its result to your Evasion against the attack.
features.short: When an attack roll against you succeeds, mark a Stress and describe how your element defends you; roll a d6 and add it to your Evasion against the attack.

features.name: Transcendence
features.rules:
Once per long rest, you can transform into a physical manifestation of your element. When you do, describe your transformation and choose two of the following benefits to gain until your next rest:
- +4 bonus to your Severe threshold
- +1 bonus to a character trait of your choice
- +1 bonus to your Proficiency
- +2 bonus to your Evasion
features.short: Once per long rest, transform into a manifestation of your element and choose two benefits until your next rest: +4 Severe threshold; +1 to a trait of your choice; +1 Proficiency; +2 Evasion.

features.name: Manipulate Magic
features.rules:
Your primal origin allows you to modify the essence of magic itself. After you cast a spell or make an attack using a weapon that deals magic damage, you can mark a Stress to do one of the following:
- Extend the spell or attack’s reach by one range
- Gain a +2 bonus to the action roll’s result
- Double a damage die of your choice
- Hit an additional target within range
features.short: After you cast a spell or make a magic-damage weapon attack, mark a Stress to do one: extend its reach by one range; +2 to the action roll’s result; double a damage die of your choice; hit an additional target within range.

features.name: Enchanted Aid
features.rules: You can enhance the magic of others with your essence. When you Help an Ally with a Spellcast Roll, you can roll a d8 as your advantage die. Once per long rest, after an ally has made a Spellcast Roll with your help, you can swap the results of their Duality Dice.
features.short: When you Help an Ally with a Spellcast Roll, roll a d8 as your advantage die. Once per long rest, after an ally’s helped Spellcast Roll, swap the results of their Duality Dice.

features.name: Arcane Charge
features.rules: You can gather magical energy to enhance your capabilities. When you take magic damage, you become Charged. Alternatively, you can spend 2 Hope to become Charged. When you successfully make an attack that deals magic damage while Charged, you can clear your Charge to either gain a +10 bonus to the damage roll or gain a +3 bonus to the Difficulty of a reaction roll the spell causes the target to make. You stop being Charged at your next long rest.
features.short: When you take magic damage, or spend 2 Hope, you become Charged. When you succeed on a magic-damage attack while Charged, clear the Charge for +10 to the damage roll or +3 to the Difficulty of a reaction roll the spell forces on the target. You stop being Charged at your next long rest.

features.name: Patron’s Mantle
features.rules: Spend a Favor to cloak yourself in a terrifying aspect of your Patron that lasts until you take Severe damage or the scene ends. While this effect is active, you gain a bonus to your damage thresholds equal to your tier and have advantage on action rolls to intimidate a target.
features.short: Spend a Favor to cloak yourself in a terrifying aspect of your Patron until you take Severe damage or the scene ends. While active, +your tier to damage thresholds and advantage on rolls to intimidate.

features.name: Deathless Embrace
features.rules: Once per rest, spend any number of Favor to roll an equal number of Patron Dice. For each result of 4 or higher, clear a Hit Point.
features.short: Once per rest, spend any number of Favor to roll that many Patron Dice. For each 4 or higher, clear a Hit Point.

features.name: Harrowing Invocation
features.rules: When an adversary targets you or an ally within Very Close range with an attack, you can spend a Favor to give them disadvantage on the roll. If the adversary fails the roll, they must also mark a Stress.
features.short: When an adversary attacks you or an ally within Very Close range, spend a Favor to give them disadvantage. If they fail, they also mark a Stress.

features.name: Damage Sink
features.rules: Once per rest, you can spend a Favor to halve incoming damage.
features.short: Once per rest, spend a Favor to halve incoming damage.

features.name: Dark Aegis
features.rules: Once per long rest when you would take damage, you can spend a Favor instead of marking Hit Points.
features.short: Once per long rest, when you would take damage, spend a Favor instead of marking Hit Points.

features.name: Draining Bane
features.rules: When an adversary targets you or an ally within Very Close range with an attack, you can spend a Favor to Drain them. When you do, they must mark a Stress, and you can clear a Stress. While Drained, the target uses a d12 instead of a d20 for attack rolls (including for advantage or disadvantage) until they fail a roll.
features.short: When an adversary attacks you or an ally within Very Close range, spend a Favor to Drain them: they mark a Stress and you can clear a Stress. A Drained target uses a d12 instead of a d20 for attack rolls (including advantage or disadvantage) until they fail a roll.

features.name: Patron’s Fury
features.rules: Spend a Favor to imbue your attacks with your Patron’s power until you deal Severe damage or the scene ends. When you roll damage while this effect is active, you also roll a number of Patron Dice equal to your tier and add their total to the damage dealt.
features.short: Spend a Favor to imbue your attacks until you deal Severe damage or the scene ends. When you roll damage while active, also roll Patron Dice equal to your tier and add their total to the damage.

features.name: Deadly Vengeance
features.rules: When you mark any number of Hit Points from an attack, you can spend a Favor to roll an equal number of Patron Dice. For each result of 4 or higher, the attacker marks a Hit Point.
features.short: When you mark Hit Points from an attack, spend a Favor to roll that many Patron Dice. For each 4 or higher, the attacker marks a Hit Point.

features.name: Menacing Reach
features.rules: Spend a Favor to increase the range of your primary weapon by one step (such as Melee to Very Close or Very Close to Close) to a maximum of Very Far range. This effect ends when you make a successful attack with that weapon.
features.short: Spend a Favor to raise your primary weapon’s range one step (Melee to Very Close, etc.), up to Very Far. It ends when you make a successful attack with that weapon.

features.name: Diminish My Foes
features.rules: When you succeed with Hope on an action roll against a target, you can spend any number of Favor to force the target to mark an equal number of Stress.
features.short: When you succeed with Hope on an action roll against a target, spend any number of Favor to make them mark that many Stress.

features.name: Fearsome Attack
features.rules: Spend a Favor to reroll any number of your damage dice. You can continue spending Favor to use this feature on the same damage roll.
features.short: Spend a Favor to reroll any number of your damage dice. You can keep spending Favor on the same damage roll.

features.name: Otherworldly Ire
features.rules: Once per rest when you take damage, you can spend any number of Favor to roll that many Patron Dice and target a number of creatures within Close range equal to the highest result. Each target must mark a Hit Point.
features.short: Once per rest, when you take damage, spend any number of Favor to roll that many Patron Dice and target creatures within Close range equal to the highest result. Each marks a Hit Point.

features.name: Courage
features.rules: When you fail a roll with Fear, you gain a Hope.
features.short: When you fail a roll with Fear, gain a Hope.

features.name: Battle Ritual
features.rules: Once per long rest, before you attempt something incredibly dangerous or face off against a foe who clearly outmatches you, describe what ritual you perform or preparations you make. When you do, clear 2 Stress and gain 2 Hope.
features.short: Once per long rest, before something incredibly dangerous or a foe who clearly outmatches you, describe your ritual or preparations, then clear 2 Stress and gain 2 Hope.

features.name: Rise to the Challenge
features.rules: You are vigilant in the face of mounting danger. While you have 2 or fewer Hit Points unmarked, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.
features.short: While you have 2 or fewer Hit Points unmarked, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.

features.name: Camaraderie
features.rules: Your unwavering bravery is a rallying point for your allies. You can initiate a Tag Team Roll one additional time per session. Additionally, when an ally initiates a Tag Team Roll with you, they only need to spend 2 Hope to do so.
features.short: Initiate a Tag Team Roll one additional time per session. When an ally initiates one with you, they spend only 2 Hope.

features.name: Slayer
features.rules: You gain a pool of dice called Slayer Dice. On a roll with Hope, you can place a d6 on this card instead of gaining a Hope, adding the die to the pool. You can store a number of Slayer Dice equal to your Proficiency. When you make an attack roll or damage roll, you can spend any number of these Slayer Dice, rolling them and adding their result to the roll. At the end of each session, clear any unspent Slayer Dice on this card and gain a Hope per die cleared.
features.short: You have a pool of Slayer Dice. On a roll with Hope, place a d6 on this card instead of gaining a Hope, up to your Proficiency in dice. When you make an attack or damage roll, spend any number of them, rolling them and adding the result. At session end, clear unspent dice and gain a Hope per die cleared.

features.name: Weapon Specialist
features.rules: You can wield multiple weapons with dangerous ease. When you succeed on an attack, you can spend a Hope to add one of the damage dice from your secondary weapon to the damage roll. Additionally, once per long rest when you roll your Slayer Dice, reroll any 1s.
features.short: When you succeed on an attack, spend a Hope to add one damage die from your secondary weapon to the damage roll. Once per long rest, when you roll Slayer Dice, reroll any 1s.

features.name: Martial Preparation
features.rules: You’re an inspirational warrior to all who travel with you. Your party gains access to the Martial Preparation downtime move. To use this move during a rest, describe how you instruct and train with your party. You and each ally who chooses this downtime move gain a d6 Slayer Die. A PC with a Slayer Die can spend it to roll the die and add the result to an attack or damage roll of their choice.
features.short: Your party gains the Martial Preparation downtime move: describe how you train with them, and you and each ally who chooses it gain a d6 Slayer Die. A PC with one can spend it to roll it and add the result to an attack or damage roll.

features.name: Herbal Remedies
features.rules: When you or an ally in the scene clears 1 or more Hit Points or Stress as the result of using a consumable, increase the number cleared by 1.
features.short: When you or an ally in the scene clears Hit Points or Stress using a consumable, increase the amount cleared by 1.

features.name: Enchanted Talisman
features.rules: Once per rest, you can imbue a small item with your protective essence. Spend any number of Hope to place an equal number of tokens on this card. When the person holding the talisman takes damage, spend a token to reduce the number of Hit Points they mark by one. Clear all tokens from this card when you take a rest.
features.short: Once per rest, imbue a small item: spend any number of Hope to place that many tokens on this card. When the holder takes damage, spend a token to reduce the Hit Points they mark by one. Clear all tokens when you rest.

features.name: Walk Between Worlds
features.rules: During a moment of calm, make a Spellcast Roll (13). Once per rest on a success, you can mark a Stress to step beyond the veil of death and converse with any nearby spirits. Place a number of tokens equal to your Spellcast trait on this card and remove one each time a spirit answers a question. When the last token is removed or at the end of the scene, you return to the Mortal Realm in the same spot you left it.
features.short: In a moment of calm, make a Spellcast Roll (13). Once per rest, on a success, mark a Stress to step beyond the veil and converse with nearby spirits. Place tokens equal to your Spellcast trait on this card and remove one each time a spirit answers. When the last is removed or the scene ends, you return to where you left.

features.name: Vexing Malison
features.rules: You have advantage on attacks against Hexed creatures.
features.short: Advantage on attacks against Hexed creatures.

features.name: Circle of Power
features.rules: Once per rest, mark a circle on the ground outlining a Very Close area around you, and place a number of tokens equal to your Spellcast trait on this card. While within this circle, you and your allies gain a +2 bonus to damage thresholds, attack rolls, and Evasion. Remove a token each time you or an ally within the circle makes an action roll or evades an attack. This spell lasts until the last token is removed or you exit the circle.
features.short: Once per rest, mark a circle outlining a Very Close area around you and place tokens equal to your Spellcast trait on this card. While in it, you and allies get +2 to damage thresholds, attack rolls, and Evasion. Remove a token each time you or an ally in it makes an action roll or evades an attack. It lasts until the last token is removed or you leave the circle.

features.name: Night’s Glamour
features.rules: Make a Spellcast Roll (13) to Glamour yourself in a bewitching facade. While Glamoured, you have advantage on rolls that leverage your illusory appearance. Additionally, adversaries within Close range must mark a Stress to attack you.
features.short: Spellcast Roll (13): Glamour yourself in a bewitching facade. While Glamoured, you have advantage on rolls that use your illusory appearance, and adversaries within Close range must mark a Stress to attack you. Unless you mark a Stress to maintain it, the Glamour drops when you mark a Hit Point or deal damage.

features.rules: Unless you mark a Stress to maintain your Glamour, it drops when you mark a Hit Point or deal damage.

features.name: Moonbeam
features.rules: Once per session, you can conjure a column of moonlight that illuminates the area within Close range until the end of the scene. While bathed in this moonlight, you and your allies gain a +1 bonus to Spellcast Rolls and can see through illusions.
features.short: Once per session, conjure a column of moonlight lighting the area within Close range until the scene ends. In it, you and allies get +1 to Spellcast Rolls and see through illusions.

features.name: Ire of Pale Light
features.rules: When a Hexed creature within Very Far range fails an attack, they must mark a Stress.
features.short: When a Hexed creature within Very Far range fails an attack, it marks a Stress.

features.name: Lunar Phases
features.rules: At the beginning of each session, roll a d6 and place it on this card. You gain the matching effect until the end of session.
features.short: At the start of each session, roll a d6 and place it on this card for the matching effect until session end: 1 New: spend a Hope to negate Minor damage; 2–3 Waxing: +2 to damage rolls; 4 Full: +3 to damage thresholds; 5–6 Waning: +1 to Evasion. Once per rest, spend a Hope to raise the die by one (a 6 becomes a 1).

features.rules: Roll Phase Effect 1 New Spend a Hope to negate Minor damage. 2 – 3 Waxing + 2 to damage rolls 4 Full + 3 to damage thresholds 5 – 6 Waning + 1 to Evasion
Once per rest, you can spend a Hope to increase the value of this die by one. If you increase the value of a 6, it becomes a 1.

features.name: Prepared
features.rules: Take an additional domain card of your level or lower from a domain you have access to.
features.short: Take an additional domain card of your level or lower from a domain you have access to.

features.name: Adept
features.rules: When you Utilize an Experience, you can mark a Stress instead of spending a Hope. If you do, double your Experience modifier for that roll.
features.short: When you Utilize an Experience, you can mark a Stress instead of spending a Hope, and double your Experience modifier for that roll.

features.name: Accomplished
features.rules: Take an additional domain card of your level or lower from a domain you have access to.
features.short: Take an additional domain card of your level or lower from a domain you have access to.

features.name: Perfect Recall
features.rules: Once per rest, when you recall a domain card in your vault, you can reduce its Recall Cost by 1.
features.short: Once per rest, when you recall a domain card from your vault, reduce its Recall Cost by 1.

features.name: Brilliant
features.rules: Take an additional domain card of your level or lower from a domain you have access to.
features.short: Take an additional domain card of your level or lower from a domain you have access to.

features.name: Honed Expertise
features.rules: When you use an Experience, roll a d6. On a result of 5 or higher, you can use it without spending Hope.
features.short: When you use an Experience, roll a d6. On a 5 or higher, use it without spending Hope.

features.name: Battlemage
features.rules: You’ve focused your studies on becoming an unconquerable force on the battlefield. Gain an additional Hit Point slot.
features.short: Gain an additional Hit Point slot.

features.name: Face Your Fear
features.rules: When you succeed with Fear on an attack roll, you deal an extra 1d10 magic damage.
features.short: When you succeed with Fear on an attack roll, deal an extra 1d10 magic damage.

features.name: Conjure Shield
features.rules: You can maintain a protective barrier of magic. While you have at least 2 Hope, you add your Proficiency to your Evasion.
features.short: While you have at least 2 Hope, add your Proficiency to your Evasion.

features.name: Fueled by Fear
features.rules: The extra magic damage from your “Face Your Fear” feature increases to 2d10.
features.short: Face Your Fear’s extra magic damage becomes 2d10.

features.name: Thrive in Chaos
features.rules: When you succeed on an attack, you can mark a Stress after rolling damage to force the target to mark an additional Hit Point.
features.short: When you succeed on an attack, mark a Stress after rolling damage to make the target mark an additional Hit Point.

features.name: Have No Fear
features.rules: The extra magic damage from your “Face Your Fear” feature increases to 3d10.
features.short: Face Your Fear’s extra magic damage becomes 3d10.

features.name: Hallowed Aura
features.rules: Once per long rest when an ally within Close range rolls with Fear, you can change it into a roll with Hope instead.
features.short: Once per long rest, when an ally within Close range rolls with Fear, change it to Hope.

features.name: Celestial Wings
features.rules: You have wings that allow you to fly. Once per scene while flying, you can spend a Hope instead of marking an Armor Slot.
features.short: You can fly. Once per scene while flying, spend a Hope instead of marking an Armor Slot.

features.name: Purposeful Design
features.rules: Decide who made you and for what purpose. At character creation, choose one of your Experiences that best aligns with this purpose and gain a permanent +1 bonus to it.
features.short: Decide who made you and why. Choose one Experience that fits; it gets a permanent +1.

features.name: Efficient
features.rules: When you take a short rest, you can choose a long rest move instead of a short rest move.
features.short: On a short rest, you can choose a long rest move instead.

features.name: Scales
features.rules: Your scales act as natural protection. When you would take Severe damage, you can mark a Stress to mark 1 fewer Hit Points.
features.short: When you would take Severe damage, mark a Stress to mark 1 fewer Hit Points.

features.name: Elemental Breath
features.rules: Choose an element for your breath (such as electricity, fire, or ice). You can use this breath against a target or group of targets within Very Close range, treating it as an Instinct weapon that deals d8 magic damage using your Proficiency.
features.short: Choose an element. Breathe on targets within Very Close range as an Instinct weapon: d8 magic damage using your Proficiency.

features.name: Thick Skin
features.rules: When you take Minor damage, you can mark 2 Stress instead of marking a Hit Point.
features.short: When you take Minor damage, mark 2 Stress instead of a Hit Point.

features.name: Increased Fortitude
features.rules: Spend 3 Hope to halve incoming physical damage.
features.short: Spend 3 Hope to halve incoming physical damage.

features.name: Stoneskin
features.rules: Gain a permanent +1 bonus to your Armor Score and damage thresholds at character creation.
features.short: Permanent +1 to Armor Score and damage thresholds at creation.

features.name: Immovable
features.rules: While you’re touching the ground, you can’t be lifted or moved against your will.
features.short: While touching the ground, you can't be lifted or moved against your will.

features.name: Quick Reactions
features.rules: Mark a Stress to gain advantage on a reaction roll.
features.short: Mark a Stress to gain advantage on a reaction roll.

features.name: Celestial Trance
features.rules: During a rest, you can drop into a trance to choose an additional downtime move.
features.short: During a rest, enter a trance to choose an additional downtime move.

features.name: Fireproof
features.rules: You are immune to damage from magical or mundane flame.
features.short: Immune to magical and mundane flame damage.

features.name: Ignition
features.rules: Mark a Stress to wreathe your primary weapon in flame until the end of the scene. While the weapon is ablaze, it gives off a bright light, and you gain a 1d6 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
features.short: Mark a Stress to set your primary weapon ablaze until scene end: bright light, and +1d6 damage with it.

features.name: Luckbender
features.rules: Once per session, after you or a willing ally within Close range makes an action roll, you can spend 3 Hope to reroll the Duality Dice.
features.short: Once per session, after you or a willing ally within Close range makes an action roll, spend 3 Hope to reroll the Duality Dice.

features.name: Wings
features.rules: You can fly. While flying, you can mark a Stress after an adversary makes an attack against you to gain a +2 bonus to your Evasion against that attack.
features.short: You can fly. While flying, mark a Stress after an adversary attacks you for +2 Evasion against that attack.

features.name: Caprine Leap
features.rules: You can leap anywhere within Close range as though you were using normal movement, allowing you to vault obstacles, jump across gaps, or scale barriers with ease.
features.short: Leap anywhere within Close range as normal movement, vaulting obstacles, gaps and barriers.

features.name: Kick
features.rules: When you succeed on an attack against a target within Melee range, you can mark a Stress to kick yourself off them, dealing an extra 2d6 damage and knocking back either yourself or the target to Very Close range.
features.short: When you succeed on a Melee attack, mark a Stress to kick off the target: +2d6 damage and knock back yourself or the target to Very Close range.

features.name: Charge
features.rules: When you succeed on an Agility Roll to move from Far or Very Far range into Melee range with one or more targets, you can mark a Stress to deal 1d12 physical damage to all targets within Melee range.
features.short: When you succeed on an Agility Roll to move from Far or Very Far into Melee range, mark a Stress to deal 1d12 physical damage to all targets within Melee range.

features.name: Unshakable
features.rules: When you would mark a Stress, roll a d6. On a result of 6, don’t mark it.
features.short: When you would mark a Stress, roll a d6; on a 6, don't.

features.name: Fungril Network
features.rules: Make an Instinct Roll (12) to use your mycelial array to speak with others of your ancestry. On a success, you can communicate across any distance.
features.short: Instinct Roll (12) to speak with others of your ancestry across any distance.

features.name: Death Connection
features.rules: While touching a corpse that died recently, you can mark a Stress to extract one memory from the corpse related to a specific emotion or sensation of your choice.
features.short: Touching a recent corpse, mark a Stress to extract one memory tied to an emotion or sensation you choose.

features.name: Shell
features.rules: Gain a bonus to your damage thresholds equal to your Proficiency.
features.short: Bonus to damage thresholds equal to your Proficiency.

features.name: Retract
features.rules: Mark a Stress to retract into your shell. While in your shell, you have resistance to physical damage, you have disadvantage on action rolls, and you can’t move.
features.short: Mark a Stress to retract into your shell: resistance to physical damage, disadvantage on action rolls, can't move.

features.name: Endurance
features.rules: Gain an additional Hit Point slot at character creation.
features.short: Additional Hit Point slot at creation.

features.name: Reach
features.rules: Treat any weapon, ability, spell, or other feature that has a Melee range as though it has a Very Close range instead.
features.short: Treat Melee range as Very Close range for any weapon, ability, spell or feature.

features.name: Nimble Fingers
features.rules: When you make a Finesse Roll, you can spend 2 Hope to reroll your Hope Die.
features.short: On a Finesse Roll, spend 2 Hope to reroll your Hope Die.

features.name: Flicker Step
features.rules: Once per scene, you can teleport to another point you can see within Far range.
features.short: Once per scene, teleport to a point you can see within Far range.

features.name: Surefooted
features.rules: You ignore disadvantage on Agility Rolls.
features.short: Ignore disadvantage on Agility Rolls.

features.name: Danger Sense
features.rules: Once per rest, mark a Stress to force an adversary to reroll an attack against you or an ally within Very Close range.
features.short: Once per rest, mark a Stress to force an adversary to reroll an attack against you or an ally within Very Close range.

features.name: Luckbringer
features.rules: At the start of each session, everyone in your party gains a Hope.
features.short: At the start of each session, everyone in your party gains a Hope.

features.name: Internal Compass
features.rules: When you roll a 1 on your Hope Die, you can reroll it.
features.short: When you roll a 1 on your Hope Die, reroll it.

features.name: High Stamina
features.rules: Gain an additional Stress slot at character creation.
features.short: Additional Stress slot at creation.

features.name: Adaptability
features.rules: When you fail a roll that utilized one of your Experiences, you can mark a Stress to reroll.
features.short: When you fail a roll using an Experience, mark a Stress to reroll.

features.name: Fearless
features.rules: When you roll with Fear, you can mark 2 Stress to change it into a roll with Hope instead.
features.short: When you roll with Fear, mark 2 Stress to change it to Hope.

features.name: Dread Visage
features.rules: You have advantage on rolls to intimidate hostile creatures.
features.short: Advantage on rolls to intimidate hostile creatures.

features.name: Feline Instincts
features.rules: When you make an Agility Roll, you can spend 2 Hope to reroll your Hope Die.
features.short: On an Agility Roll, spend 2 Hope to reroll your Hope Die.

features.name: Retracting Claws
features.rules: Make an Agility Roll to scratch a target within Melee range. On a success, they become temporarily Vulnerable.
features.short: Agility Roll to scratch a target within Melee range; on a success, they become temporarily Vulnerable.

features.name: Sturdy
features.rules: When you have 1 Hit Point remaining, attacks against you have disadvantage.
features.short: At 1 Hit Point remaining, attacks against you have disadvantage.

features.name: Tusks
features.rules: When you succeed on an attack against a target within Melee range, you can spend a Hope to gore the target with your tusks, dealing an extra 1d6 damage.
features.short: When you succeed on a Melee attack, spend a Hope to gore the target for an extra 1d6 damage.

features.name: Amphibious
features.rules: You can breathe and move naturally underwater.
features.short: Breathe and move naturally underwater.

features.name: Long Tongue
features.rules: You can use your long tongue to grab onto things within Close range. Mark a Stress to use your tongue as a Finesse Close weapon that deals d12 physical damage using your Proficiency.
features.short: Grab things within Close range. Mark a Stress to use it as a Finesse Close weapon: d12 physical damage using your Proficiency.

features.name: Natural Climber
features.rules: You have advantage on Agility Rolls that involve balancing and climbing.
features.short: Advantage on Agility Rolls to balance and climb.

features.name: Nimble
features.rules: Gain a permanent +1 bonus to your Evasion at character creation.
features.short: Permanent +1 to Evasion at creation.

features.name: Gale Force
features.rules: Mark a Stress to conjure a gust of wind that carries you or a Very Close ally up to Very Far range.
features.short: Mark a Stress to carry yourself or a Very Close ally on a gust up to Very Far range.

features.rules: Additionally, you can always control the speed at which you fall.
features.short: You can always control the speed at which you fall.

features.name: Eye of the Storm
features.rules: Spend 2 Hope to grant you or an ally within Melee range a +1 bonus to Evasion until you take Severe damage or you use this feature again.
features.short: Spend 2 Hope to give yourself or an ally within Melee range +1 Evasion until you take Severe damage or use this again.

features.name: Amphibious
features.rules: You can breathe and move naturally underwater.
features.short: Breathe and move naturally underwater.

features.name: Lifespring
features.rules: Once per rest when you have access to a small amount of water, you can mark a Stress to clear a Hit Point on yourself or an ally within Very Close range.
features.short: Once per rest with a little water on hand, mark a Stress to clear a Hit Point on yourself or an ally within Very Close range.

features.name: Oasis
features.rules: During a short rest, you or an ally can reroll a die used for a downtime move and take the higher result.
features.short: On a short rest, you or an ally can reroll a downtime move die and take the higher result.

features.name: Unbound
features.rules: Once per session when you roll with Fear, you can change it into a roll with Hope instead.
features.short: Once per session, when you roll with Fear, change it to Hope.

features.name: Hardy
features.rules: When you take a rest, you clear a Hit Point.
features.short: When you take a rest, clear a Hit Point.

features.name: Close-Knit
features.rules: Once per long rest, you can spend any number of Hope to grant an ally within Far range an equal number of Hope.
features.short: Once per long rest, spend any number of Hope to give an ally within Far range that many Hope.

features.name: Privilege
features.rules: You have advantage on rolls to consort with nobles, negotiate prices, or leverage your reputation to get what you want.
features.short: Advantage on rolls to consort with nobles, negotiate prices, or leverage your reputation.

features.name: Well-Read
features.rules: You have advantage on rolls that involve the history, culture, or politics of a prominent person or place.
features.short: Advantage on rolls involving the history, culture, or politics of a prominent person or place.

features.name: Dedicated
features.rules: Record three sayings or values your upbringing instilled in you. Once per rest, when you describe how you’re embodying one of these principles through your current action, you can roll a d20 as your Hope Die.
features.short: Record three sayings or values from your upbringing. Once per rest, when your action embodies one, roll a d20 as your Hope Die.

features.name: Found Family
features.rules: Once per rest, you can spend a Hope to use an ally’s Experience as if it were your own. When you do so, describe how your time with that ally prepared you for this moment.
features.short: Once per rest, spend a Hope to use an ally's Experience as your own, describing how they prepared you for this moment.

features.rules: When you join a new community or rediscover your old one, you can permanently trade this card for that one instead.
features.short: When you join a new community or rediscover your old one, you can permanently trade this card for it.

features.name: Steady
features.rules: You have advantage on rolls to traverse dangerous cliffs and ledges, navigate harsh environments, and use your survival knowledge.
features.short: Advantage on rolls to traverse dangerous cliffs and ledges, navigate harsh environments, and use survival knowledge.

features.name: Know the Tide
features.rules: You can sense the ebb and flow of life. When you roll with Fear, place a token on your community card. You can hold a number of tokens equal to your level. Before you make an action roll, you can spend any number of these tokens to gain a +1 bonus to the roll for each token spent. At the end of each session, clear all unspent tokens.
features.short: When you roll with Fear, place a token on your community card (max your level). Before an action roll, spend any number of tokens for +1 each. Clear unspent tokens at session end.

features.name: Scoundrel
features.rules: You have advantage on rolls to negotiate with criminals, detect lies, or find a safe place to hide.
features.short: Advantage on rolls to negotiate with criminals, detect lies, or find a safe place to hide.

features.name: Low-Light Living
features.rules: When you’re in an area with low light or heavy shadow, you have advantage on rolls to hide, investigate, or perceive details within that area.
features.short: In low light or heavy shadow, advantage on rolls to hide, investigate, or perceive details there.

features.name: Nomadic Pack
features.rules: Add a Nomadic Pack to your inventory. Once per session, you can spend a Hope to reach into this pack and pull out a mundane item that’s useful to your situation. Work with the GM to figure out what item you take out.
features.short: Add a Nomadic Pack to your inventory. Once per session, spend a Hope to pull a useful mundane item from it (work with the GM).

features.name: Brave Face
features.rules: Once per session when you would be forced to mark a Stress, you can spend a Hope instead..
features.short: Once per session, when you would mark a Stress, spend a Hope instead.

features.name: Lightfoot
features.rules: Your movement is naturally silent. You have advantage on rolls to move without being heard.
features.short: Your movement is silent. Advantage on rolls to move without being heard.

domainCards.name: Rune Ward
domainCards.rules:
You have a deeply personal trinket that can be infused with protective magic and held as a ward by you or an ally. Describe what it is and why it’s important to you. The ward’s holder can spend a Hope to reduce incoming damage by 1d8.
If the Ward Die result is 8, the ward’s power ends after it reduces damage this turn. It can be recharged for free on your next rest.
domainCards.short:
A personal trinket infused with protective magic, held as a ward by you or an ally. The holder can spend a Hope to reduce incoming damage by 1d8.
If the Ward Die result is 8, the ward’s power ends after it reduces damage this turn. It recharges for free on your next rest.

domainCards.name: Unleash Chaos
domainCards.rules:
At the beginning of a session, place a number of tokens equal to your Spellcast trait on this card.
Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Far range and spend any number of tokens to channel raw energy from within yourself to unleash against them. On a success, roll a number of d10s equal to the tokens you spent and deal that much magic damage to the target. Mark a Stress to replenish this card with tokens (up to your Spellcast trait).
At the end of each session, clear all unspent tokens.
domainCards.short:
At the start of a session, place {{spellcast|# tokens|tokens equal to your Spellcast trait}} on this card.
Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Far range, spending any number of tokens: on a success, roll d10s equal to the tokens spent and deal that much magic damage. Mark a Stress to refill tokens (up to {{spellcast|#|your Spellcast trait}}).
At the end of each session, clear unspent tokens.

domainCards.name: Wall Walk
domainCards.rules: Spend a Hope to allow a creature you can touch to climb on walls and ceilings as easily as walking on the ground. This lasts until the end of the scene or you cast Wall Walk again
domainCards.short: Spend a Hope to let a creature you touch climb walls and ceilings as easily as walking on the ground. Lasts until the end of the scene or you cast Wall Walk again.

domainCards.name: Cinder Grasp
domainCards.rules:
Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Melee range. On a success, the target instantly bursts into flames, takes 1d20+3 magic damage, and is temporarily lit On Fire.
When a creature acts while On Fire, they must take an extra 2d6 magic damage if they are still On Fire at the end of their action.
domainCards.short:
Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Melee range. On a success, the target bursts into flames, takes 1d20+3 magic damage, and is temporarily On Fire.
A creature acting while On Fire takes an extra 2d6 magic damage if still On Fire at the end of their action.

domainCards.name: Floating Eye
domainCards.rules: Spend a Hope to create a single, small floating orb that you can move anywhere within Very Far range. While this spell is active, you can see through the orb as though you’re looking out from its position. You can transition between using your own senses and seeing through the orb freely. If the orb takes damage or moves out of range, the spell ends.
domainCards.short: Spend a Hope to create a small floating orb you can move anywhere within Very Far range. You can see through it and switch freely between its sight and your own. The spell ends if the orb takes damage or moves out of range.

domainCards.name: Counterspell
domainCards.rules: You can interrupt a magical effect taking place by making a reaction roll using your Spellcast trait. On a success, the effect stops and any consequences are avoided, and this card is placed in your vault.
domainCards.short: Interrupt a magical effect with a reaction roll using your Spellcast trait. On a success, the effect stops, its consequences are avoided, and this card is placed in your vault.

domainCards.name: Flight
domainCards.rules: Make a Spellcast Roll (15). On a success, place a number of tokens equal to your Agility on this card (minimum 1). When you make an action roll while flying, spend a token from this card. After the action that spends the last token is resolved, you descend to the ground directly below you.
domainCards.short: Make a Spellcast Roll (15). On a success, place {{agilityMin1|# tokens|tokens equal to your Agility (minimum 1)}} on this card. Spend a token when you make an action roll while flying. After the action that spends the last token, you descend to the ground directly below you.

domainCards.name: Blink Out
domainCards.rules: Make a Spellcast Roll (12). On a success, spend a Hope to teleport to another point you can see within Far range. If any willing creatures are within Very Close range, spend an additional Hope for each creature to bring them with you.
domainCards.short: Make a Spellcast Roll (12). On a success, spend a Hope to teleport to a point you can see within Far range. Spend an additional Hope for each willing creature within Very Close range to bring them along.

domainCards.name: Preservation Blast
domainCards.rules: Make a Spellcast Roll against all targets within Melee range. Targets you succeed against are forced back to Far range and take d8+3 magic damage using your Spellcast trait.
domainCards.short: Make a Spellcast Roll against all targets within Melee range. Targets you succeed against are forced back to Far range and take d8+3 magic damage using your Spellcast trait.

domainCards.name: Chain Lightning
domainCards.rules: Mark 2 Stress to make a Spellcast Roll, unleashing lightning on all targets within Close range. Targets you succeed against must make a reaction roll with a Difficulty equal to the result of your Spellcast Roll. Targets who fail take 2d8+4 magic damage. Additional adversaries not already targeted by Chain Lightning and within Close range of previous targets who took damage must also make the reaction roll. Targets who fail take 2d8+4 magic damage. This chain continues until there are no more adversaries within range.
domainCards.short: Mark 2 Stress to make a Spellcast Roll, unleashing lightning on all targets within Close range. Targets you succeed against make a reaction roll (Difficulty = your Spellcast Roll result) and take 2d8+4 magic damage on a failure. The chain repeats on adversaries not yet targeted within Close range of previous targets who took damage, until none remain.

domainCards.name: Premonition
domainCards.rules: You can channel arcane energy to have visions of the future. Once per long rest, immediately after the GM conveys the consequences of a roll you made, you can rescind the move and consequences like they never happened and make another move instead.
domainCards.short: Once per long rest, immediately after the GM conveys the consequences of a roll you made, rescind the move and consequences and make another move instead.

domainCards.name: Rift Walker
domainCards.rules:
Make a Spellcast Roll (15). On a success, you place an arcane marking on the ground where you currently stand. The next time you successfully cast Rift Walker, a rift in space opens up, providing safe passage back to the exact spot where the marking was placed. This rift stays open until you choose to close it or you cast another spell.
You can drop the spell at any time to cast Rift Walker again and place the marking somewhere new.
domainCards.short:
